messages:
katie: Heads-up — starting a design thread for AWS KMS integration for Redwood Private (VPC) control-plane + data-plane. Goal: envelope encryption pattern, rotation story, RBAC for key usage, audit logging, and incident recovery playbook. Any immediate red flags? cc @samir @julian @irene

samir: +1. quick notes: control-plane should store only wrapped DEKs (ciphertext blobs). data-plane can cache decrypted DEKs in memory with short TTLs. never persist plaintext DEKs to disk.

julian: Agreed. Proposed pattern: customer CMK (KEK) in their account. We store per-object DEK encrypted by that CMK in control-plane DB: dek_wrapped. Data-plane asks control-plane for dek_wrapped, requests rewrap/decrypt via customer's KMS (via cross-account role) and caches result in memory for request handling.

irene: Cross-account access is the trick. We should avoid granting our account direct key access where possible. Preferred: customer creates an IAM role we assume (sts:AssumeRole) with kms:Decrypt/kms:ReEncrypt* on the CMK ARN. Alternative: customer can create a KMS grant for our principal, but grants are harder to audit from their side.

katie: Draft key policy + example IAM role + create-grant CLI below. feedback?

samir: sample key policy (customer side) — keep it minimal and scoped to the CMK ARN:
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "AllowRedwoodControlPlane",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-controlplane"},
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:ReEncrypt*", "kms:DescribeKey"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```
CLI create-grant example for short-lived grant (customer runs):
```bash
aws kms create-grant --key-id alias/redwood-cmk --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-controlplane --operations Decrypt ReEncryptFrom ReEncryptTo --name "redwood-grant"
```

julian: Rotation plan notes: do NOT auto-rotate CMKs without customer consent. For DEKs we manage, implement periodic rewrap (server-side): use ReEncrypt API to rewrap DEK ciphertext under the latest CMK version. Worker job picks unrewrapped items, calls kms:ReEncrypt, updates DB. Add idempotency tokens and backoff for KMS ThrottlingException.

irene: Add CloudTrail + KMS Data events to the onboarding checklist. Ensure KMS:Decrypt and ReEncrypt events are forwarded to our central SIEM for alerting. Also log the IAM role/sts:AssumeRole actor for traceability.

katie: RBAC specifics for our service principal — sample IAM statement to attach to the customer role we assume:
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:ReEncrypt*", "kms:DescribeKey"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111111111111:key/abcd-1234-efgh"
    }
  ]
}
```
Keep the resource restrictive (no wildcard across account).

samir: Operational tuning: KMS has API rate limits. For large-scale rewraps, implement a rate-limited worker pool and exponential backoff. Also consider batching re-encrypts per customer to avoid sudden spikes.

matt: Incident response flow for suspected key compromise: 1) Immediately disable the compromised CMK (SetKeyState/DisableKey) 2) Revoke grants (if grants used) 3) Switch affected customers to a recovery KEK (pre-provisioned recovery CMK under customer control or emergency-managed CMK) and rewrap DEKs under the recovery key 4) Rotate DEKs and rotate application credentials. Open ticket, preserve CloudTrail/KMS logs for forensics.

julian: Add note — rewrap/reencrypt will fail if CMK already disabled. So step order matters. If suspected compromise, disable only after establishing recovery rewrap path or you'll orphan data.

irene: For audit + compliance — require customers to enable CloudTrail kms:DataEvents and to share the trail (or forward logs) to us read-only for a 90-day window. We need exact principal + API call for forensic timelines.

katie: BYOK / CloudHSM customers: key material may be in a custom key store. Latency and availability differ. Our onboarding wizard must check KeyState and key store connectivity and surface failover guidance.

samir: Small perf optimization: if you have high QPS per small model, consider using KMS grants for a limited time window and operations to avoid repeated network roundtrips; grants let a principal perform Decrypt locally (still KMS-backed) with fewer permission checks. Note grants are tied to key and principal and must be revoked or will be invalidated when CMK is changed.

julian: Edge-case: rewrap large tenant with millions of DEKs — do a rolling approach by object partition, snapshot progress, checkpoint, resume. Track rewrap_version metadata on each object.

ops-bot: deploy-bot created incident runbook: "KMS-compromise-playbook" (link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kms-compromise) — ticket #SEC-2026-84 created.

matt: Also ensure we keep an encrypted backup of DEK ciphertexts in S3 with server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) under a recovery key. Backups are immutable snapshots used only for recovery, rotated and access-controlled.

irene: Tests we need before GA: 1) Simulate CMK disable & recovery rewrap 2) Throughput test for re-encrypt jobs with KMS throttling 3) End-to-end audit log verification and SIEM ingestion 4) RBAC negative tests (ensure role without kms:Decrypt fails)

katie: I'll produce a short playbook and onboarding checklist by EOD Fri. Thanks for the input! :tada:

samir: adding a doc link that helped our testing: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/overview.html

julian: small caution — don't log raw ciphertexts in plaintext logs. store only metadata keys, key ids, and truncated hashes.

katie: perfect. follow-up sprint ticket incoming.
